island-park.summary: Island Park sits almost entirely in unincorporated Fremont County (the incorporated city itself is a famously thin ~500-ft-wide, 33-mile strip). Idaho House Bill 583 (effective July 1, 2026) now preempts the county's former commercial-permit regime for STRs, leaving one of the lightest-touch regulatory environments in the state — the main live risk is private HOA covenants, not government rules.
permitResidency: Permit / license required? No, as of July 1, 2026 — state law bars any county STR-specific license, fee, permit, certification, or registration. Fremont County previously ran a Class I commercial Transient Lodging Permit ($200/$500 by guest capacity, plus septic/well inspection every 2 years); this is now superseded, though it is unconfirmed whether the county has formally struck it from its code.
Primary residence required? No — owner-occupancy mandates are barred statewide; whole-home, non-owner-occupied STRs are fully permitted.
operatingLimits: No caps, quotas, or unit-per-parcel limits — density and spacing restrictions are barred by state law.
Occupancy: only generally-applicable International Building Code residential limits may be enforced, the same as any home.
Taxes: 6% Idaho sales tax + 2% state Travel & Convention Tax = 8% total. No local-option or auditorium-district tax found for Island Park (zip 83429 shows the state rate only).
investorNotes: STRs are now a "non-transient residential use" by state law — allowed anywhere ordinary residential use is allowed, no special resort/recreation zoning category.
Required safety equipment only: smoke alarms, CO detectors, fire extinguisher, egress ladders. No STR-specific inspection may be required.

Enforcement is now complaint-driven (noise/nuisance/parking) — the Idaho Association of Counties has publicly noted that without a registry, counties can no longer proactively verify safety compliance.

HOA risk is real and litigated here: North Henry's Lake v. Norton (Idaho Supreme Court, 2026) upheld a pre-existing Fremont County HOA's STR ban under Idaho Code §55-3211 (new bans need the owner's written consent; old ones are grandfathered) — check covenants per property.
Airbnb/Vrbo auto-collect and remit state taxes on platform bookings; direct-booking hosts must register with the Idaho State Tax Commission themselves.

sources.title: Idaho State Tax Commission — Travel & Convention Tax

teton-valley.summary: Teton County, Driggs, Victor, and Tetonia each ran different STR regimes before 2026 — Driggs and Victor materially stricter than the county or Tetonia. Idaho House Bill 583 (effective July 1, 2026) has now largely flattened those differences into a single permissive state floor; local lodging-tax rate is the main thing that still varies by jurisdiction.
permitResidency: Permit / license required? No, statewide, as of July 1, 2026. Driggs previously charged an $80 initial / $50 annual STR permit with a mandatory Fire Marshal inspection; Victor required its own STR business license. Both are being wound down — Driggs held a June 2026 hearing to rewrite its code, though it's unconfirmed whether either city has fully scrubbed the old fee from its books.
Primary residence required? No, anywhere in the valley — owner-occupancy mandates are barred statewide.
operatingLimits: No numeric caps — Driggs' roughly one-STR-per-property limit (2022 workforce-housing ordinance) is preempted.
Occupancy: generally-applicable IBC-based limits only.

Taxes: 8% state baseline (6% sales + 2% Travel & Convention). Driggs and Victor each add an 8% local lodging tax (Driggs raised its rate January 2026) — roughly 16% combined in those two cities. Unincorporated Teton County and Tetonia show no local-option tax, likely 8% total.
investorNotes: Teton County's own Planning & Zoning FAQ now shows no zoning permit requirement for short- or long-term rentals except Bed & Breakfasts/campgrounds — consistent with winding the old septic-tied county permit down.
Required safety equipment only (smoke alarms, CO/fire extinguisher per floor, escape ladders); no STR-specific inspection may be mandated statewide.
Hailey-style unit-splitting rules don't apply here, but Driggs' AMD26-2 rewrite (June/July 2026) is worth re-checking for final adopted text.

HOA covenants are unaffected by state law: Idaho Code §55-3211 requires written owner consent for new rental bans (pre-existing restrictions remain enforceable). Most Teton Valley subdivisions predate STRs and don't restrict them (e.g. Shoshoni Plains near Grand Targhee explicitly allows rentals), but this varies by subdivision.

sources.title: City of Victor — Short Term Rental Information

mccall-west-central-mountains.summary: McCall ran the most detailed STR permit system found anywhere in this research — the 2026 legislature specifically targeted it. Donnelly, Cascade, and unincorporated Valley County were always lighter-touch. All four are now bound by the same permissive state floor, but McCall's own repeal is still visibly in progress, so this region reads as transitional rather than settled.
permitResidency: Permit / license required? No, statewide, as of July 1, 2026 — though McCall's own site confirms it "will be repealing many of the codes regarding Short-Term Rentals ... effective July 1, 2026," implying the old permit (business license + signed compliance declaration) was still active up to that date. Donnelly's per-parcel business license and the county's administrative permit are also now preempted; no confirmation either has formally amended its code.
Primary residence required? No — none of the four jurisdictions ever required owner-occupancy, and it's barred statewide regardless.
operatingLimits: No cap, waitlist, or lottery was ever found for McCall despite that being a common assumption — it was a permit-for-every-operator system, not scarcity-based, and is preempted either way.
McCall's old occupancy formula (bedrooms×2+2, capped at 10 without a conditional-use permit) and its annual fire-safety inspection are being eliminated.

Taxes: 8% state baseline. McCall adds a 7% city Local Option Tax (roughly 15% combined) — the highest of the four. Donnelly adds 4% (roughly 12%), Cascade 1% (roughly 9%). Unincorporated Valley County shows no local add-on.
investorNotes: McCall prevailed in a 2025 lawsuit upholding its old STR ordinance, then saw much of that same ordinance preempted by the legislature months later — an unusual sequence worth knowing about if researching the city's own public statements.
Cascade has the thinnest documentation of the four — no dedicated STR ordinance was found at all; treat it as the lightest-regulated of the group.
Required safety equipment only going forward (smoke alarms, extinguisher, CO detector, escape ladders); the old annual McCall Fire & EMS inspection is being wound down.

The Payette Lake shoreline has numerous platted subdivisions with private CC&Rs — HOA-level STR restrictions are a well-documented pattern in comparable mountain-lake markets and plausible here, though not individually verified.

sources.title: City of Donnelly — Local Option Tax

coeur-dalene.summary: As recently as mid-2025, Coeur d'Alene ran a genuinely restrictive STR permit system with a 35-unit cap. A 2025 Idaho Supreme Court ruling and the 2026 state preemption law have since stripped that framework down; the region (Coeur d'Alene, Hayden, Post Falls, Harrison, and unincorporated Kootenai County) now reads uniformly permissive at the government level.
permitResidency: Permit / license required? No, statewide, as of July 1, 2026 — Coeur d'Alene's own annual, non-transferable STR permit (parking plan, safety checklist, 24/7 responsible-party requirement) is preempted, though it's unconfirmed whether Council has finished a formal code rewrite. No dedicated STR ordinance was found for Hayden, Post Falls, or Harrison.
Primary residence required? No — Coeur d'Alene's ADU-specific owner-occupancy condition is preempted; no other jurisdiction in the cluster required it.
operatingLimits: Coeur d'Alene's 35-unit citywide cap on non-owner-occupied STRs (already recommended for removal by P&Z in December 2025 following the Lava Hot Springs ruling) is now barred by state law regardless.
Occupancy: IBC-based limits only, applied the same as to any residence.

Taxes: 8% state baseline. Coeur d'Alene, Hayden, and Post Falls have no local-option lodging tax (population over the 10,000 resort-city threshold) — 8% total. Harrison, a qualifying resort city, layers a 1% Local Option Tax (roughly 9%, if lodging is included in that base).
investorNotes: Unincorporated Kootenai County has no STR-specific chapter found; vacation rentals appear to be treated as an ordinary residential/accessory use, though individual septic-system capacity (Panhandle Health District) can functionally cap guest counts on unincorporated lakefront parcels.
Required safety equipment only (smoke alarms, CO detector/floor, extinguisher, escape ladders); Coeur d'Alene's legacy "safety checklist" was self-certified, not an in-person inspection.
Much of the Lake Coeur d'Alene shoreline sits inside HOA-governed developments — private CC&R restrictions are unaffected by state preemption and are a live per-property diligence item.
This is a fast-moving area of law: as recently as mid-2025 this specific city would have rated Moderate-to-Restrictive. Re-verify before relying on it for a transaction.

sources.title: Idaho Assoc. of REALTORS v. City of Lava Hot Springs — NAR case summary
City of Coeur d'Alene — Short-Term Rentals

boise-foothills-eagle.summary: Boise ran an active, evolving STR license regime from 2019 until repealing it in May 2026 specifically to comply with the state's new preemption law. Meridian, Eagle, and unincorporated Ada County never had comparably strict rules. Because this cluster's revenue is driven by a small number of large foothills/Eagle homes, HOA status is likely the more binding real-world constraint today.
permitResidency: Permit / license required? No — the City of Boise's own Clerk page confirms its STR-specific business license was repealed effective May 18, 2026, "to align with changes in Idaho state law," ahead of the July 1 statewide deadline. No STR-specific ordinance was confirmed for Meridian, Eagle, or unincorporated Ada County (a new Title 8 zoning code, ~January 2025, predates the state law).
Primary residence required? No — not required anywhere in this cluster.
operatingLimits: No caps or density limits in any of the four jurisdictions.
Occupancy: IBC-based limits only.

Taxes: 8% state baseline, plus a 5% Greater Boise Auditorium District room tax (explicitly applies to STR-marketplace bookings) covering a large part of Boise, all of Garden City, and portions of Meridian/Eagle — roughly 13% combined inside the district, 8% outside it. Foothills and outlying Eagle parcels may sit outside the district boundary; check the parcel-level lookup.
investorNotes: Boise continues ordinary nuisance/noise/parking/safety enforcement post-repeal, the same as for any residence — no STR-specific compliance mechanism remains since no license exists to revoke.

The Idaho Association of Counties has publicly flagged that eliminating STR registries statewide makes proactive safety-equipment enforcement harder — expect complaint-driven enforcement going forward.

The Boise foothills and much of Eagle contain numerous HOA-governed subdivisions (large-lot estates, golf-course/equestrian communities, master-planned Eagle developments) where HOAs commonly restrict STRs independent of public law — likely the binding constraint for this cluster's larger, higher-revenue homes.
This is a very new law (in force ~2.5 months at verification); even its own sponsors reportedly called it imperfect, with a possible legislative revisit in 2027.

sources.title: City of Boise — Short-Term Rental License

sun-valley-wood-river.summary: Ketchum ran the most developed STR framework in the Wood River Valley (permit, mandatory inspection, a one-per-parcel cap, a 2-night minimum) and is mid-rewrite to comply with state law. Sun Valley, Hailey, and unincorporated Blaine County were already effectively hands-off. A more permissive bill that would have let cities require permits for "professional" operators (SB 1263) was considered and did not pass.
permitResidency: Permit / license required? No, statewide, as of July 1, 2026. Ketchum's ~$500/property annual permit and mandatory Fire District inspection are being eliminated per a mid-2026 code rewrite; whether the city's legacy one-per-parcel cap and 2-night minimum survived that rewrite is unconfirmed. Sun Valley never adopted an STR ordinance (voluntary safety guidance only, since 2022). Hailey requires standard tax/business registration, not an STR-specific permit.
Primary residence required? No, anywhere in the valley.
operatingLimits: Ketchum's cap and minimum-stay rules, if not already repealed, are preempted regardless. No caps found in Sun Valley, Hailey, or unincorporated Blaine County.
Hailey's one notable surviving local rule: on a lot with both a primary home and an ADU, only one of the two units may operate short-term — untested against the state's equal-treatment standard.

Taxes: 8% state baseline. Ketchum adds a 3% lodging Local Option Tax (roughly 11%; a further increase was under discussion for a 2026 ballot, outcome unconfirmed). Sun Valley adds 4% (roughly 12%). Hailey's stacked local taxes total roughly 4% (roughly 12% combined). Unincorporated Blaine County has no local-option tax.
investorNotes: Ketchum's post-rewrite safety-equipment standard moves to self-certification rather than a Fire District walkthrough.

Condo associations and subdivisions across the valley (Sun Valley's Elkhorn/Warm Springs-area complexes, Ketchum condo buildings, Hailey subdivisions) commonly impose their own minimum-stay or rental bans via private CC&Rs — unaffected by state preemption.
Verify Ketchum's final adopted ordinance text directly before relying on cap/minimum-stay specifics — this research could not confirm the post-rewrite text.
Whether Airbnb/Vrbo automatically collect each city's local-option tax (versus just the 8% state layer) was not independently confirmed — check platform tax settings.

sources.title: City of Sun Valley — Local Option Tax
City of Hailey — Accessory Dwelling Units

sandpoint-pend-oreille.summary: Sandpoint had a 35-unit cap on non-owner-occupied STRs until early 2026 and publicly resisted the state's new preemption law longer than most Idaho cities. Unincorporated Bonner County (including Sagle) ran a lighter administrative-permit system. Both are now bound by the same permissive state floor; the real remaining difference between them is tax rate, not legality.
permitResidency: Permit / license required? No, statewide, as of July 1, 2026 — though Sandpoint's City Council deadlocked 4-4 on formally repealing its own STR ordinance in May 2026 and deliberately slowed adoption while objecting to the state law; final repeal was not confirmed complete as of the most recent reporting found (legally unenforceable regardless). Bonner County's Vacation Rental Permit (County Code §12-484) is similarly preempted but unconfirmed as formally amended. Sandpoint separately still runs a Short-Term Rental Occupancy Tax Permit — a tax-collection registration, not an operating permit, which remains valid.
Primary residence required? No — Sandpoint's old owner-occupied/non-owner-occupied distinction (with 200-ft neighbor notification for non-owner-occupied units) is preempted.
operatingLimits: Sandpoint's 35-unit cap on non-owner-occupied STRs was voluntarily removed in February 2026 after litigation threats, and is barred by state law regardless.
Bonner County's old occupancy formula (tied to bedrooms and parking spaces) is preempted; only IBC-based limits may now apply.

Taxes: 8% state baseline. Sandpoint adds a 14% Resort City Occupancy Tax (raised from 7% in 2023, approved through 2035) — roughly 22% combined, among the highest in Idaho. Unincorporated Bonner County (Sagle, etc.) has no local-option tax — roughly 8% total.
investorNotes: Lake Pend Oreille has numerous platted lakefront subdivisions in both Sandpoint and Sagle where HOA/CC&R rental restrictions are a plausible, common friction point independent of public law.
Required safety equipment only going forward; STR-specific inspections and neighbor-notification rules are barred.

Sandpoint's public pushback against the state law (a divided Council, a deliberately slow-walked repeal process) makes this a jurisdiction worth re-checking directly before a transaction — the practical/enforcement gap between state law and local administrative posture may be wider here than elsewhere.
Whether Bonner County's parking-tied occupancy formula remains enforceable in any form is unclear, since it differs from the IBC-based standard state law now requires.

sources.title: City of Sandpoint — Resort City Tax / STR Occupancy Tax
Bonner County Daily Bee — Sandpoint HB 583 coverage

lava-hot-springs.summary: Lava Hot Springs' own zoning ordinance was struck down by the Idaho Supreme Court in 2025 for confining non-owner-occupied STRs to commercial zones; the 2026 statewide preemption law then went further. The city passed a narrower safety-focused ordinance just before that law took effect. Unincorporated Bannock County appears to have no STR-specific rules at all.
permitResidency: Permit / license required? Historically yes — the city's old business-license requirement was the subject of the litigated case (Idaho Assoc. of REALTORS v. City of Lava Hot Springs, decided May 2025). The city passed Ordinance 2026-005 in May 2026 (safety requirements only, not a licensing gate) about six weeks before the state's July 1, 2026 preemption took effect; whether the old business-license requirement itself has been formally repealed is unconfirmed.
Primary residence required? No — the Supreme Court struck down the owner-occupied-only zoning rule, and owner-occupancy mandates are separately barred statewide.
operatingLimits: A 13% citywide cap was under internal city consideration in a 2025 planning memo but never confirmed enacted, and would be barred by state law regardless.
Occupancy: IBC-based limits only.

Taxes: 8% state baseline, plus a reported 3% local hotel-motel/STR occupancy tax (roughly 11% combined) — a ballot measure to raise this to 5% was reportedly floated around 2024–2025; outcome unconfirmed, treat 3% as the best-available current rate.
investorNotes: No STR-specific provisions were found for unincorporated Bannock County — the surrounding county may simply never have needed rules given the small unincorporated population near Lava.
A July 2025 city planning memo referenced 29 licensed STRs plus an estimated 5+ unlicensed, out of ~197 total housing units — useful market-context baseline, not a current legal requirement.

Required safety equipment only under Ordinance 2026-005 (smoke alarms, extinguishers, escape ladders, occupancy limits); exact penalty schedule and full ordinance text were not independently confirmed.
Whether individual listings sit inside city limits or unincorporated Bannock County was not determined for this research — verify per property, since only the city has documented rules.

sources.title: Idaho Assoc. of REALTORS v. City of Lava Hot Springs — NAR case summary
Lava Hot Springs city planning memo (2025-07-06)
Idaho State Tax Commission — Travel & Convention Tax

bear-lake.summary: Fish Haven and St. Charles, on the Idaho shore of Bear Lake, are both unincorporated — Bear Lake County is the only government with authority, and it has essentially no published STR-specific rules. The real constraint here is private: a confirmed shorefront HOA (Bear Lake West) bans STRs outright, and that ban legally survives state preemption.
permitResidency: Permit / license required? No — no dedicated STR permit, registration, or business-license process is published on the county's site, and state law now bars adding one. 2026 legislative testimony referenced an STR-specific asphalt-driveway requirement attributed to the county, but the underlying ordinance (if any) could not be located and would be unenforceable regardless.
Primary residence required? No — not required, and barred statewide.
operatingLimits: No caps or density limits found or permitted.
Occupancy: IBC-based limits only — notable given local reporting has described some older farmhouses hosting 60–80 people, well beyond any reasonable limit, with real septic-capacity strain.
Taxes: 8% state baseline only (6% sales + 2% Travel & Convention). No county-level or local-option lodging tax exists — unincorporated communities can't levy Idaho's resort-city tax.
investorNotes: Bear Lake West, a residential community in Fish Haven, has an outright STR ban in its governing documents (adopted to protect shared amenities from large-group use). Idaho Code §55-3211 grandfathers pre-existing HOA restrictions, so this ban survives state preemption — a property inside Bear Lake West cannot legally operate as an STR regardless of how permissive county/state law is.
Other shorefront HOAs were not identified in this research; check per-property before assuming any Bear Lake listing is unrestricted.
Required safety equipment only (smoke alarms, extinguisher, CO detector, escape ladders); no dedicated county inspection program was found.
An Idaho-side property owes only Idaho taxes (8%) regardless of Utah-based marketing or management, even though the lake and its tourism economy straddle both states.

sources.title: Utah Public Radio — Bear Lake STR/HOA reporting
Bear Lake County Planning and Zoning

garden-valley.summary: Garden Valley is unincorporated, so Boise County's general zoning/building code is the applicable framework — no STR-specific permit or license program was ever found here. The small nearby City of Crouch has no STR ordinance either. This is Idaho's statewide-preemption floor with essentially no local layer on top of it.
permitResidency: Permit / license required? No — no evidence Boise County ever ran an STR-specific permit or license program (unlike, e.g., the City of Boise, a distinct and unrelated jurisdiction despite the similar name). Whether a generic county business license incidentally applies to STR operators is unconfirmed.
Primary residence required? No — not required, and barred statewide regardless.
operatingLimits: No caps, density limits, or spacing rules found or permitted.
Occupancy: generally-applicable IBC-based limits only.
Taxes: 8% state baseline only (6% sales + 2% Travel & Convention). No local-option tax was found for Garden Valley or Crouch — neither appears on the state's list of cities levying one.
investorNotes: The City of Crouch (pop. ~150–185) publishes only water, firearms-discharge, and fireworks ordinances — no STR content; relevant only to the handful of properties actually inside its city limits.
Required safety equipment only (smoke alarms, extinguisher, CO detector, escape ladders); no inspection regime found or permitted.

Garden Valley has at least some HOA-governed subdivisions (e.g. Mountain View Place, Country Living Estates) where private covenants could still restrict STR use independent of the permissive public-law backdrop — check per subdivision.
This is a small rural county with thin public documentation and almost no enforcement track record yet under the new state law — absence of a published rule isn't strong evidence there truly is none.
